text:
yovoice 
 Give your words a voice. Compose your ideas into songs. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 English · 简体中文 

 Website · CLI & Agent Skill · API / MCP Deployment · Development 

---

yovoice is an open-source, local-first audio and music creation studio for macOS, Windows and Linux. 

Turn text into expressive speech, natural cloned voices, complete vocal songs, and multi-track scores right on your machine. Featuring zero-shot voice cloning, emotional performance controls, AI music generation with lyrics, and General MIDI score arranging— all running 100% locally with zero cloud API calls, zero per-character fees, and zero Python environment headaches. 

 

---

 Why yovoice?

- 🔒 100% Local Privacy : Runs entirely on your local GPU/CPU. Your manuscripts, reference voices, and creations never leave your computer.
- 💸 Zero Recurring Fees : Say goodbye to per-character/per-minute meters and expensive cloud voice/music subscriptions.
- ⚡ Native C++ Performance (No Python Hell) : Powered by audio.cpp v0.9.3. Ships with bundled Windows CUDA 12.4/13.3 runtimes and native macOS Metal support. Double-click and create—no Conda or PyTorch conflicts.
- 🎛️ Creator Workstation : Multi-take versioning for side-by-side comparison, waveform trimming, timeline scrolling, and clean stems/MIDI export.
- 🤖 MCP & AI Agent Ecosystem : Chat with DeepSeek, Qwen, Claude, OpenAI, or local Ollama to create and edit works end to end. Includes a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Cursor and Claude Code.

---

 Features

- Speech, voice design and cloning — clone a reference voice, design a voice from a description, adjust emotion and delivery, and edit takes on a timeline.
- Story dubbing — import text or subtitle files, assign a character to each line, and generate line by line.
- Transcribe and subtitles — turn audio or video into timed subtitle lines and export SRT / WebVTT, fill in a reference transcript automatically, or export aligned subtitles for a speech version.
- Music — write a style and lyrics with section markers, then generate songs or instrumentals with ACE-Step 1.5, or songs and score-based instrumentals with YuE2, or instrumental music and sound effects from an English description with Stable Audio 3; the playback page syncs lyrics to the vocals. Separate any song into six stems and mix them in the stem studio, or transcribe it to multi-instrument MIDI.
- Score — write parts by bar and beat, import MIDI or let an Agent compose, render with a General MIDI sound font, and export MIDI and stems. See Score.
- Optional AI service — the built-in assistant panel chats with DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama or any compatible API and acts on your works: it writes arrangements and lyrics, edits text, assigns voices and starts generation; keys stay on this computer. See AI service.
- 12 interface languages — English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, 한국어, Español, Français, Deutsch, Português (Brasil), Русский, Italiano and Tiếng Việt; switch anytime in Settings, no restart needed.

---

 Supported Models

 Use Models 
 --- --- 
 Voice cloning and emotion IndexTTS 2.0 / 2.5, Qwen3-TTS Base 
 Voice design and cloning VoxCPM2, OmniVoice, Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign, Breeze TTS 2, Ming 3.0 TTS 
 More voice cloning XTTS v2 (17 languages), Plapre 3 (Danish), Fish Audio Drama 3 (speaker and event tags), Audio8 TTS Realistic (11 languages) 
 Built-in voices Kokoro-82M, Qwen3-TTS CustomVoice, Voxtral 4B TTS, Gradium Phonon 
 Songs and instrumentals ACE-Step 1.5 Turbo / XL Turbo, YuE2 3B 
 Instrumentals and sound effects Stable Audio 3 Small Music / Small SFX / Medium 
 Speech recognition and subtitles Qwen3 ASR 0.6B / 1.7B, Confucius4-R2T2, Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 
 Stems, MIDI and lyric alignment HTDemucs 6-stem, BS-RoFormer, MuScriptor, Lyric Aligner, SheetSage2 

All models are downloaded inside the App or with the CLI. See model selection for file sizes, hardware requirements, inputs and examples. OmniVoice, YuE2, Breeze TTS 2, Voxtral 4B TTS and MuScriptor weights are restricted to non-commercial use; XTTS v2 and Drama 3 use their own Coqui and Fish Audio licenses; Stable Audio 3 is free below USD 1M annual revenue under the Stability AI Community License.

---

 Installation

Choose the package for your platform from the repository’s Releases tab or visit the official website.

 Platform Package Install 
 --- --- --- 
 macOS 14+ · Apple Silicon .dmg Open the disk image and drag yovoice to Applications 
 Windows 10/11 · x64 -setup.exe Run the installer, then open yovoice from the Start menu 
 Windows 10/11 · x64 · NVIDIA GPU -cuda12.4-setup.exe Bundles the CUDA 12.4 runtime; works with older GPUs and drivers and uses the GPU from first launch 
 Windows 10/11 · x64 · NVIDIA GPU -cuda13.3-setup.exe Bundles the CUDA 13.3 runtime; needs a newer driver, smaller download 
 Linux · x64 (Debian/Ubuntu) -linux-x64.deb sudo apt install ./yovoice- -linux-x64.deb , then open yovoice from the application menu 
 Linux · x64 (other distributions) -linux-x64.tar.gz Extract and run ./install.sh to add yovoice to the application menu for the current user 

The Windows installer downloads and installs WebView2 Runtime if needed. Models are downloaded inside the app; uninstalling preserves user data in /.yovoice .

On Linux the app needs WebKitGTK 4.1 ( libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 on Debian/Ubuntu, webkit2gtk4.1 on Fedora, webkit2gtk-4.1 on Arch); the .deb installs it automatically. Linux runs on the CPU out of the box, and a Vulkan GPU runtime can be downloaded in Settings → Inference engine. The Linux app doesn't update itself yet; download new versions from Releases.

Check for updates from the app menu on macOS or Windows. Updates are also checked and downloaded in the background; restart to install when ready. Windows updates download only the app ( -update.exe ) and keep the installed runtime; when a release recommends a newer runtime you can upgrade it in Settings → Inference engi

On Linux the app needs WebKitGTK 4.1 (libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 on Debian/Ubuntu, webkit2gtk4.1 on Fedora, webkit2gtk-4.1 on Arch); the .deb installs it automatically. Linux runs on the CPU out of the box, and a Vulkan GPU runtime can be downloaded in Settings → Inference engine. The Linux app doesn't update itself yet; download new versions from Releases.

Check for updates from the app menu on macOS or Windows. Updates are also checked and downloaded in the background; restart to install when ready.
